title: How to use Linear for developers on Mac: a guide for managing your workflow
metaTitle: Linear for developers on Mac: workflow tips and Lazur integration
description: Master Linear for developers on Mac with these practical tips and learn how Lazur helps you navigate your project management tasks.
intro: Linear for developers on Mac is a high-performance tool that keeps your project tracking fast and keyboard-focused. You can use Lazur to stay in your flow while managing issues, cycles, and projects without leaving your terminal or editor.
tldr: Linear is a fast, keyboard-first tool for software teams.
Developers spend 84 percent of their time on non-coding tasks like planning.
Lazur helps you navigate Linear by answering questions and pointing at UI elements.
Use keyboard shortcuts to keep your hands on the home row.
The Linear Mac app requires macOS 12 or later.

blocks.text: Why Linear for developers on Mac is a standard

Linear is built for speed. It uses an Electron wrapper on macOS that feels native. It avoids the bloat of older project tools. Developers like it because it respects their time. You can perform almost any action with a key press. This keeps you in the zone. You do not need to reach for your mouse for every status change.

The Mac app is not on the Mac App Store. You download it from the official site. It requires macOS 12 or later. Once installed, it integrates with your system notifications. This helps you stay updated on code reviews and issue assignments. It also keeps your browser cleaner by moving project management to its own window.

Research shows developers spend most of their day on tasks other than writing code. You spend time in meetings, planning, and documentation. Linear helps manage this overhead. By keeping your issues organized, you reduce the time lost to context switching. A well-maintained backlog is a map for your day.

items: Use C to create a new issue instantly.
Press Cmd + K to open the command palette for any action.
Use P to cycle through priority levels.
Press ? to see the full list of keyboard shortcuts.
Use G then I to jump to your inbox.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you in Linear

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It sees your screen when you hold Option + Command. If you get lost in a complex project view, ask Lazur where your current cycle is. It will draw a circle around the UI element. You do not need to hunt for menus.

You can also ask Lazur how to do specific tasks. If you forget the shortcut to create a sub-issue, ask Lazur. It will guide you through the process one click at a time. It does not click for you, but it shows you the path. This builds your muscle memory over time.
Common mistakes developers make in Linear

Many teams try to force Linear to act like older tools. They create too many status columns. This leads to clutter. Keep your workflow simple. Use cycles to track progress over time. Do not over-engineer your boards. If a team has more than two teams, you might need to upgrade from the free plan.

Another mistake is ignoring the command palette. Everything you need is in Cmd + K. Do not use your mouse to move issues between projects. Search for the issue and move it using the palette. This saves seconds every time. Over a week, those seconds add up to hours of regained focus.
If you are struggling with a complex view, create a saved filter. Use the filter bar to set your criteria and save it to your sidebar. This makes returning to your specific view a one-click action.

blocks.text: Integrating Linear into your Mac stack

Linear works best when it is part of your daily rhythm. Keep it open in a dedicated space. Use your Mac mission control to switch between your editor and Linear. If you use Raycast, you can even install extensions to interact with Linear from your launcher. Combine these tools to build a fast, reliable environment.

Developers often use tools like Ghostty for their terminal and OrbStack for containers. These tools are fast and native to macOS. Linear fits this stack well. It does not lag. It does not hog memory. It is a tool that stays out of your way while you work.

Once you master the basics, look into labels and templates. Labels help you categorize work by type or team. Templates help you standardize issue creation. If you find yourself typing the same issue description, create a template. This ensures all necessary info is included every time.

Bulk actions are also powerful. Select multiple issues by holding Command and clicking. Then press Cmd + K to apply a change to all of them at once. This is great for moving issues to a new cycle or updating their status after a meeting.

faq.question: Is Linear available on the Mac App Store?
faq.answer: No, you must download the Linear desktop app directly from the official Linear website.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside the Linear app?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works in any app on your Mac. You can ask it questions about your Linear workspace while the app is open.

faq.question: What is the best way to learn Linear shortcuts?
faq.answer: Press ? inside the Linear app at any time to open the complete, searchable list of keyboard shortcuts.

faq.question: Can I use Linear for free?
faq.answer: Yes, Linear has a free plan that supports unlimited members, but it is limited to two teams and 250 non-archived issues.
